L01 | | A dusty spirit board sits on the round parlor table beside a cold, cobwebbed hearth, its wooden pointer marked A and D restin' between HELLO and GOODBYE. Reckon it is just waitin' on your hands.
O01 | Lay our fingertips on the pointer and ask if anyone is here.
O02 | Recall how a sitting like this is properly conducted.
O03 | Leave the board alone for now.
L02 | | You rest your fingertips light on the wood and ask one plain question at a time. Whatever listens in the dark spells its mind out letter by letter.
L03 | | Best mind your knuckles, though, for the dead can bite back with aclimbing chill. Once that pointer touches GOODBYE, the board goes deaf and dumb for good.
L04 | | You scratch around in your memory for parlor tricks and church-yard tales. All you come up with is a mouthful of dust and half a rumor.
L05 | | Your fingertips settle on the wood, and the pointer gives a dry little shiver. Over in the cold hearth, a low flame catches with a crackle, and the whole room leans in close.
L06 | | HELLO.
L07 | | The pointer stops dead on the last letter, patient as an old house servant awaitin' the bell. A thin, cellar cold settles into the pads of your fingers.
O04 | Who are you?
O05 | Who did this to you?
O06 | Where are Phillip and Adela?
O07 | Who is behind all of this?
O08 | How do we get out of here, and what opens the way?
O09 | Where is the door to the attic?
O10 | Who is the grey cat upstairs?
O11 | What is that big red dog on the third floor?
O12 | That is enough. Let us bid him goodbye.
L08 | | The wood scrapes out from under your stillness, draggin' itself across the painted alphabet one slow letter at a time.
L09 | | JOSEPH PATRINI. BUTLER.
L10 | | I SERVED THIS HOUSE. I KEEP MY POST.
L11 | | The pointer balks and catches on the grain, then jerks hard across the board like a mule pulled by the bit.
L12 | | EUSTACE LOCKWOOD. MY MASTER.
L13 | | HE SLEW US ALL.
L14 | | The little wooden heart lifts a hair off the varnish and settles down square over YES.
L15 | | ABOVE. ALIVE. NOT FOR LONG.
L16 | | The pointer drifts in a slow, wide circle through the dust before it settles on a letter.
L17 | | A HAG. IN THE ATTIC.
L18 | | SHE CRAVES THEIR SOULS. THIS HOUSE HUNTS FOR HER.
L19 | | The pointer swings sharp from corner to corner, quick and neat as a clerk tallyin' a ledger.
L20 | | SIX KEEPSAKES OPEN THE WAY.
L21 | | GEM. KEY. CUP. DOLL. BEAR. PIN.
L22 | | THEY REST ON EVERY FLOOR. GATHER THEM ALL.
L23 | | The wood creeps an inch, then darts straight across the varnish without a speck of hesitation.
L24 | | TROPHIES.
L25 | | LOOK UP.
L26 | | The pointer shivers under your nails like a bare foot steppin' onto frosted iron.
L27 | | LIAR.
L28 | | HE HUNGERS FOR TALES. DO NOT FEED HIM.
L29 | | The wood slows right down and glides gentle across the painted arc, soft as a hand on a cradle.
L30 | | SALLY.
L31 | | THE LITTLE ONE RUNS FREE NOW. SHE IS THIS HOUSE.
L32 | | The pointer settles back still, and the draft stays down in the floorboards where it belongs. The board just waits on your next word.
L33 | | The pointer bucks hard under your palms. A thin needle of winter cold runs straight through every hand on the wood.
L34 | | The board kicks back colder this time, sendin' a gray frost up past your wrists until your fingers go thick and numb.
L35 | | That third chill bites deep into the meat of your thumbs. It settles like hard pond ice inside the bones of every hand.
L36 | | The cold snaps up your arms and wrings the warm wind right out of your chests. Your stiff fingers scarce want to uncurl from the wood.
L37 | | A black frost locks every arm to the elbow in a vice of winter iron. It holds you fast a long count before it lets go slow.
L38 | | Reckon if you let the old fellow go now, this board ain't gonna speak twice. Whatever you leave unasked stays buried in the dark.
O13 | Wait. Let us ask something else first.
O14 | Let him go.
L39 | | Before you can lift your hands away, the pointer gives a sharp, hasty tug under your fingers.
L40 | | SIX KEEPSAKES OPEN THE WAY. GEM. KEY. CUP. DOLL. BEAR. PIN.
L41 | | SEARCH EVERY FLOOR. FIND THEM FIRST.
L42 | | Right before your fingers part from the wood, the pointer scrapes out one hasty warning.
L43 | | A HAG WAITS IN THE ATTIC.
L44 | | STOP HER WORK. MAKE HASTE.
L45 | | Just as you go to raise your hands, the pointer darts out with a sharp, urgent tap.
L46 | | THE WAY UP IS HIDDEN. TROPHIES.
L47 | | LOOK TO THE CEILING.
L48 | | Before your fingers clear the varnish, the little wooden heart tugs back hard for one last word.
L49 | | SHE WEARS THE LADY'S FACE.
L50 | | DO NOT TRUST YOUR EYES. LOOK TWICE.
L51 | | The pointer trembles in place a spell, like a man holdin' back a heavy word at the door.
L52 | | ONE THING MORE. MY SON LIVES.
L53 | | FRANCIS. PLEASE FIND HIM.
L54 | | TELL HIM HIS NAME. PATRINI.
L55 | | GOODBYE.
L56 | | The pointer slides down to the corner and stops dead. Over in the hearth, the fire hisses out like a doused lamp, takin' the chill with it.
L57 | | Only dust sits on the painted letters now, cold and still under your hands. Some doors in this world only open the once.
